newsitem.title: USA: Dow seen up at open as defensive issues draw favor.
newsitem.headline: Dow seen up at open as defensive issues draw favor.

text.p: The Dow industrials are expected to continue their run into record territory on Friday, as new signs of slowing economic growth has enhanced investor interest in mega-cap and defensive stocks.

The most recent signs of tapering economic growth included Thursday's tame industrial production and capacity data as well as a fall-off in housing starts. The data triggered a rally in bonds that has continued early this morning, pushing long-term yields down near 6.75 percent.

Analysts said the data has also prompted a rally in shares in the pharmaceutical and consumer products sectors at the expense of technology shares. The result has been two straight Dow record closes despite declines in the technology-laden Nasdaq Composite, a trend analysts saw continuing.
"I'd expect a continuation of what we've been seeing," said Hildegard Zagorski, market analyst at Prudential Securities. "It looks like there's been a shift to defensive stocks and out of the techs."
"Of course, this will last until the next economic report that suggests otherwise," she added.

An August international trade balance report represents the only economic data due at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT. Economists forecast the trade deficit will drop to about $8.5 billion from July's surprisingly high $11.7 billion.
Analysts generally do not expect the report to have much market impact.

"Unless there is a ballooning in the deficit, the bond market is going to make an attempt on 6.75 percent or even 6.70 percent," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments. "That should set the stage for a higher open."
Today is also a double-witching options expiration day, but analysts predicted little in the way of market impact.
In Tokyo, stocks closed higher ahead of Sunday's general election. The Nikkei Average rose 189 points at 21,612.
In London, U.S. stocks were generally firm. The FTSE 100 Index gained 19 points to 4061.
The dollar was steady at just about 112 yen in Tokyo and barely off its highs in Europe, holding above 1.54 marks.
U.S. Treasuries were higher, with the long bond up 13/32 to yield 6.77 percent.
The S&P 500 index future rose 1.7 points to 712.7.

The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street examines the recently completed share offering of Controladora Comercial Mexicana SA. The column writes that investors bought up the shares, which debuted on the NYSE last week, at a time when retailing is among the riskiest of Mexican stock plays.
The New York Times Market Place notes that Wall Street offered a tepid greeting to the announced merger deal between Tenet Healthcare Corp and OrNda HealthCorp.
